TEST RESULTS (all passing, including this story’s tests),- Jest run (`npm test -- --verbose`) shows all suites passing, including: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts – "Require Story Annotation Rule (Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS)" - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts – "Require Req Annotation Rule (Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS)" - tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts – "annotation-checker helper" (Story 003.0 TS support) - tests/rules/require-story-helpers*.test.ts, require-story-io.*.test.ts (Story 003.0 edge cases and IO helpers) - tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts (verifies both rules in presets)
CORE RULE IMPLEMENTATIONS,require-story-annotation rule implementation:,File: src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - Declares the rule with traceability to this story: /** * ESLint rule module: require-story-annotation * @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md * ... * @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED */ - meta: - type: "problem" - docs.description: "Require @story annotations on functions ..." - hasSuggestions: true - fixable: "code" - messages.missingStory: clear, actionable message including an example story path - schema: single options object with - scope: array of strings, enum: DEFAULT_SCOPE - exportPriority: enum: EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES - create(context): - Reads options: scope (defaults to DEFAULT_SCOPE), exportPriority (defaults to "all") - Uses shared helper shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority) from src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - Delegates visitor construction to buildVisitors(context, sourceCode, { shouldProcessNode, scope, exportPriority }) from src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts
require-req-annotation rule implementation:,File: src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - Header traces to this story and requirements: /**** * Rule to enforce @req annotation on functions * @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md * @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED * @req REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION * @req REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT * @req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE * @req REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY */ - meta: - type: "problem", fixable: "code" - docs.description: "Require @req annotations on function-like exports ..." - messages.missingReq: clear, imperative guidance and example - schema: identical structure to require-story-annotation (scope array, exportPriority enum, additionalProperties: false) - Options type shares the same semantics: type Options = [{ scope?: (typeof DEFAULT_SCOPE)[number][], exportPriority?: (typeof EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES)[number] }?]; - create(context): - Uses DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES imported from require-story-helpers - Derives scope with same semantics: if scope not provided or empty, fallback to DEFAULT_SCOPE - Derives exportPriority with same semantics, defaulting to "all" - shouldCheck(node) wraps shared shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority) - runCheck(node) calls shared checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false }) - Returns listeners for: - FunctionDeclaration - FunctionExpression (skipping when parent is MethodDefinition) - MethodDefinition - TSDeclareFunction - TSMethodSignature All use runCheck, so both rules operate on the same set of function-like constructs when in scope.
FUNCTION DETECTION & SCOPE (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY),Shared helpers for function detection and scope:,File: src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts - DEFAULT_SCOPE: export const DEFAULT_SCOPE: string[] = [ "FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction", ]; -> Matches exactly the story’s required function-like constructs; arrow functions are not in this default set. - EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES = ["all", "exported", "non-exported"]
File: src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - isExportedNode(node): walks parent chain for ExportNamedDeclaration / ExportDefaultDeclaration; - shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority): - Returns false if node.type not in scope - Determines export status via isExportedNode - Applies exportPriority logic: - "exported": only exported nodes - "non-exported": only non-exported nodes - "all": any in-scope node - These helpers are used: - In require-story-annotation via a local should(node) calling shouldProcessNode - In require-req-annotation via shouldCheck(node) calling shouldProcessNode
Verification by tests (for both rules):,File: tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - Valid cases include: - FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, class MethodDefinition (TS), TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature with @story - Arrow function explicitly allowed when unannotated by default: name: "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED] unannotated arrow function allowed by default", code: `const arrowFn = () => {};` - exportPriority behavior: - Valid: unexported function ignored when exportPriority: "exported" - Valid: exported arrow function missing @story allowed when exportPriority: "exported" (still excluded) - Invalid: exported function missing @story gets an error and an autofix suggestion - scope behavior: - Valid: arrow function ignored when scope: ["FunctionDeclaration"] - Invalid: FunctionDeclaration missing annotation reported when scope is ["FunctionDeclaration"]
File: tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - Valid function types with @req: - FunctionDeclaration - FunctionExpression - MethodDefinition - TS FunctionExpression in variable declarator (including exported) - Invalid cases ensure detection on same constructs: - Missing @req on FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, anonymous IIFE, MethodDefinition (class and object), TS FunctionExpression (regular and exported) - Scope configuration: - Valid: FunctionExpression ignored when scope only includes FunctionDeclaration - Invalid: FunctionDeclaration still reported when scope only includes FunctionDeclaration - exportPriority configuration (REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY): - Non-exported function ignored when exportPriority == 'exported' - Exported function required when exportPriority == 'exported' - Exported function ignored and non-exported required when exportPriority == 'non-exported' - Similar tests for methods and FunctionExpressions
Arrow functions excluded by default:,require-story-annotation visitors (src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts) include ArrowFunctionExpression, but: - buildArrowFunctionVisitor() uses options.shouldProcessNode(node) - DEFAULT_SCOPE does NOT include "ArrowFunctionExpression" - shouldProcessNode returns false for ArrowFunctionExpression unless scope is explicitly extended (but scope schema and docs do not allow ArrowFunctionExpression) => In practice, ArrowFunctionExpression handlers never report by default, matching "Arrow functions are excluded by default". - require-req-annotation has no ArrowFunctionExpression visitor at all, so arrow functions are also excluded there.
ANNOTATION ENFORCEMENT (REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED),require-story-annotation rule behavior:,Tests: tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - Invalid tests confirm enforcement: - Missing @story on FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, class method all: - yield errors with messageId: "missingStory" - provide autofix output adding `/** @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md */` before the function - Backward compatibility: unannotated plain function still invalid under multi-story support
Implementation details for reporting and autofix:,File: src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node): robust detection via - jsdocHasStory (uses sourceCode.getJSDocComment) - commentsBeforeHasStory (uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore) - leadingCommentsHasStory - linesBeforeHasStory (scans previous lines for @story/@supports) - parentChainHasStory (walks parent nodes) - fallbackTextBeforeHasStory (scans text window before node) - Wrapped in try/catch for safety -> graceful error handling - resolveTargetNode: chooses correct AST node to attach annotation (e.g. interface for TSMethodSignature, export wrapper, etc.) - extractName: walks node and parents to derive function/method name or "(anonymous)". - reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget): - Skips if hasStoryAnnotation is true - Resolves target node via resolveTargetNode - Chooses nameNode as the Identifier for id/key when available - context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingStory", data: { name, functionName: name }, fix: createAddStoryFix(target), suggest: [{ desc: `Add JSDoc @story annotation...`, fix: createAddStoryFix(target) }] }) - Satisfies REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED and REQ-ERROR-LOCATION (error at function name).
File: src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts - createAddStoryFix(target) and createMethodFix(node) insert ANNOTATION (`/** @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md */`) before proper location.
Error message quality verified:,File: tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts - Constructs synthetic AST and runs rule.create(context) manually - Asserts: - message template exists and contains the {{name}} placeholder - error.messageId === 'missingStory' - error.data === { name: 'bar', functionName: 'bar' } - suggestion.desc is precise and includes example with this story’s path - suggestion.fix is defined => Confirms REQ-ERROR-LOCATION, REQ-ERROR-MSG-ACTIONABLE and overall UX.
require-req-annotation behavior (REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED, REQ-JSDOC-PARSING, REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT):,File: src/utils/annotation-checker.ts & src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options): - Obtains sourceCode from context - Collects: - jsdoc via getJsdocComment(sourceCode, node) - leading comments via getLeadingComments(node) - commentsBefore via getCommentsBefore(sourceCode, node) - Combines comments and passes jsdoc + comments (+ context,node) into hasReqAnnotation - If hasReqAnnotation is false, invokes reportMissing(context, node, enableFix) - hasReqAnnotation(...): - If sourceCode+node available, runs advanced heuristics: - linesBeforeHasReq(sourceCode, node) - parentChainHasReq(sourceCode, node) - fallbackTextBeforeHasReq(sourceCode, node) - Guards all operations with defensive checks and try/catch - Fallback: inspects jsdoc.value and comment values for '@req' OR '@supports' - Accepts both @req and @supports as satisfying requirement presence (REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS) - reportMissing(context, node, enableFix = true): - Derives name via getNodeName and falls back to "(anonymous)" - Chooses nameNode as id or key identifier where possible, else node - context.report with: messageId: 'missingReq', data: { name, functionName: name } optional fix: createMissingReqFix(node) when enableFix=true - createMissingReqFix(node): - Uses getFixTargetNode to attach JSDoc appropriately (methods, variable declarators, expression statements) - Inserts `/** @req */\n` before chosen node
Tests confirming behavior:,File: tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts - Uses helper rule that delegates TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature to checkReqAnnotation - Valid cases: - TSDeclareFunction with @req - TSMethodSignature with @req - Invalid cases assert: - Missing @req on TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature - Autofix output inserting `/** @req */` in correct locations
File: tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - Valid: - Only @req, @story+@req combinations, @supports-only accepted (REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS) - Various function expressions and methods across JS/TS - Invalid: - Functions and methods without @req, including TS variants and anonymous expressions - Uses missingReq helper to assert consistent error payload { name, functionName } => Together, enforce that any in-scope function has a @req annotation, satisfying REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED.
JSDOC / COMMENT PARSING STRATEGY (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING),Both rules rely on centralized parsing helpers rather than ad hoc parsing: - For @story: - jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory - linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory in require-story-io.ts - For @req: - getJsdocComment, getLeadingComments, getCommentsBefore, combineComments in annotation-checker.ts - hasReqAnnotation with analogous heuristics (linesBefore, parentChain, fallback text)
In both cases: - JSDoc is retrieved via sourceCode.getJSDocComment - Leading and preceding comments are combined and scanned - Fallbacks inspect surrounding source text using a bounded window - Guards and try/catch ensure malformed comments or missing APIs do not throw => This matches the story’s requirement for a common, robust strategy for extracting annotations from JSDoc/comments, even though story and req use separate helper modules.
INTEGRATION & PRESETS (AC: Integration, DOD: Rule integrated into plugin presets),File: src/index.ts - RULE_NAMES includes both rules: const RULE_NAMES = [ "require-story-annotation", "require-req-annotation", ... ]; - Dynamic loader populates rules[name] for each, with error fallback - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps both rules to 'error': { "traceability/require-story-annotation": "error", "traceability/require-req-annotation": "error", ... } - createTraceabilityFlatConfig() returns flat config using those severities - configs.recommended and configs.strict both include that flat config
File: tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts - Asserts rules object contains both 'require-story-annotation' and 'require-req-annotation' - Asserts configs.recommended and configs.strict map both rules to 'error'
File: tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts - Uses FlatESLint with plugin presets - Lints `function foo() {}` and `function bar() {}` - Verifies that traceability/require-story-annotation is triggered (and by configuration, require-req-annotation is also registered in the same presets) => Confirms integration with ESLint flat config and mixed JS/TS environments.
DOCUMENTATION (AC: Documentation),File: docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md - @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - Documents: - Purpose: enforce @story annotations for traceability - Supported node types: FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature - Options: scope array and exportPriority, with JSON schema and examples - Examples for JS and TS, including correct and incorrect cases.
File: docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md - @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - Documents: - Purpose: enforce @req on functions/methods - Supported node types (same list as above) - Notes that arrow functions are not checked (aligns with story requirement) - Options scope/exportPriority identical in semantics to require-story-annotation - Provides examples in JS and TS including correct and incorrect patterns.
ERROR HANDLING & EDGE CASES (AC: Error Handling),For @story detection:,File: src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts - All helpers guard against missing APIs and malformed nodes (e.g., missing loc, invalid range) and return false rather than throwing. - fallbackTextBeforeHasStory wraps slicing in try/catch and treats failures as "no annotation".
File: src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - hasStoryAnnotation wraps entire heuristic chain in try/catch and returns false on failure, so linting never crashes.
Edge-case tests:,File: tests/rules/require-story-helpers-edgecases.test.ts - Verify: - jsdocHasStory returns false when JSDoc exists but value not string - commentsBeforeHasStory returns false when comments value not string - leadingCommentsHasStory handles various shapes - resolveTargetNode behaves correctly in ExpressionStatement and export scenarios - shouldProcessNode respects exportPriority options.
File: tests/rules/require-story-io.edgecases.test.ts - Verify that helpers safely handle missing source.lines, missing node.loc, missing getText, invalid node.range, etc.
For @req detection:,File: src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts - linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq all have: - Strict type/shape checks - Graceful returns on invalid state - try/catch guards around sourceCode text operations - hasReqAnnotation wraps advanced heuristics in try/catch; on failure it falls back to simple jsdoc/comments scanning.
TOGETHER ENFORCING BOTH @story AND @req WHEN BOTH RULES ENABLED,From configuration (src/index.ts) and docs: - Both rules are part of the default recommended/strict presets with severity 'error'. - Behavior tests show: - require-story-annotation enforces @story on the required function-like nodes - require-req-annotation enforces @req on the same kinds of nodes, with identical scope/exportPriority semantics => When both rules are active in a project (as they are by default in presets), a function-like construct in scope without @story will fail require-story-annotation, and without @req will fail require-req-annotation, satisfying the story’s "together" requirement.
traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements in docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are implemented and verified: - Both ESLint rules `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` exist, share the same function-detection scope (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature), and apply consistent `scope` and `exportPriority` semantics. - Arrow functions are excluded from enforcement by default. - Both rules use centralized helpers to parse JSDoc and surrounding comments for their annotations, with robust, guarded logic and additional heuristics (line scanning, parent-chain scanning, fallback text windows). - Missing annotations are enforced with clear, actionable error messages and precise error locations at function identifiers (including TS nodes), and both rules support TypeScript-specific constructs. - Extensive Jest test coverage (RuleTester suites and helper tests) explicitly reference this story and its REQ IDs, and all tests pass. - Documentation for both rules is present, story-linked, and describes behavior, options, supported node types, and examples, matching the specification. - The plugin’s recommended/strict presets integrate both rules with severity `error`, so enabling the presets ensures that in-scope functions must carry both @story and @req when both rules are turned on.
Given this concrete implementation and passing tests, this story is fully implemented and is marked PASSED.
